clue.text: Vespa, say, is no longer 2 parking

parts.note: something that is no longer simply was
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A remark that the Vespa scooter can no longer be parked somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Vespa looks like the Italian scooter, but it is the Latin genus name of the hornets and their kin. The stray '2' is a printing artefact with no job.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespa is the zoological genus of hornets, so a Vespa is an example of the stinging insect.

clue.text: Bikini possibly, for which there's a charge

explanation.surface: A swimsuit that you have to pay to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is the Pacific coral island, not the swimsuit. Split as A TOLL, the second half is something you pay for passing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a ring-shaped coral reef island in the Pacific, and a toll is a fee charged for using a road or bridge.

clue.text: Bird, perhaps initially a migrant in flight

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word perhaps
letters in flight are scattered and rearranged, so the words a migrant are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A bird spotted in the air, which may be a migrating one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in flight' rearranges A MIGRANT into TARMIGAN, after P from 'perhaps'. The surface sense of flight as flying is the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, a species of game bird.

clue.text: Be difficult to control in a higher 3 position?

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaving after being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: In British office usage, to act up is to fill a more senior post temporarily; the other sense is to misbehave. The '3' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: To misbehave is to be unruly, and acting up in British workplaces means temporarily doing a superior's job.

clue.text: Quite some time? It's conjecturally more than half a year

definitions.text: It's conjecturally more than half a year

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time, guessed at as over six months.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, about thirty Sundays at one a week spans some thirty weeks, more than half a year; the idiom simply means a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a very long period, and read literally thirty-odd Sundays cover more than twenty-six weeks.

clue.text: Perhaps Earl Grey's ready to throttle King, showing perfidy

indicators.note: throttling grips something round the neck, so one piece closes around the other

parts.note: Earl Grey is an example of tea, and when it is ready the tea's on
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An aristocrat named Grey strangling a monarch, an act of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey looks like a nobleman but is the tea, giving TEA'S ON, which wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery against one's sovereign or country is a form of betrayal or bad faith.

clue.text: Images of people deemed suitable for hanging

definitions.text: Images of people deemed suitable for hanging

parts.words: Images of people deemed suitable for hanging
parts.note: suggests criminals fit for the gallows but means likenesses of people hung on the walls of a museum

explanation.surface: Pictures of people judged to deserve execution.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanging is meant as displaying on a wall, not execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum room or building devoted to painted likenesses of people hung for display.

clue.text: Promote luxurious 4 material (line discontinued)

indicators.note: a line discontinued is one taken away, so the letter for line is dropped

parts.note: plush is a rich fabric with a long soft nap

explanation.surface: Advertising an opulent fabric that is no longer made.
explanation.walkthrough: '(line discontinued)' looks like a shop note about a withdrawn product; it drops the L from PLUSH. The '4' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: To push a product or idea is to advance or advertise it energetically.

clue.text: Better holding in rising terror

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from bottom to top
holding means the first word grips the next one within it

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Better to stay in when terror is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'rising' are both container-and-direction signals; in a down entry 'rising' reads the letters upwards, so the reversal turns a word for better that grips 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming fear is alarm or terror.

clue.text: Discarded material from Fight Club

parts.note: a scrap is an informal word for a fight
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Something thrown out from the film or group Fight Club.
explanation.walkthrough: Fight Club reads as the film title, but it is two pieces: a scrap and a golf iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste metal thrown away for recycling is junk metal.

clue.text: Vague shot at nothing? It could be chipped

parts.note: a potshot is a random shot, so a vague shot is a pot
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A random attempt to hit nothing, which might be chipped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chipped' suggests a golf chip shot, carrying on the shooting picture, but it means cut into chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A spud is cut into strips to make fries, British chips.

clue.text: King and artist blocking doorway, 6 wandering aimlessly

indicators.note: blocking a doorway means standing within it, so these go inside

parts.note: an entry is a doorway or way in
R stands for rex, Latin for king
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A monarch and a painter standing in the doorway while drifting about.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6' is a printing artefact with no job.
explanation.definitionFit: Errantry is roving in search of adventure, like a knight-errant's travels.

clue.text: Flowering plant seen in 7 a variety of climates

indicators.note: a variety suggests a different form, so the word climates is rearranged

explanation.surface: A flower that grows in many different climates.
explanation.walkthrough: The '7' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing vine with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Ready to accept city's 8 set of instructions

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city getting a set of instructions it is ready to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: EC1 to EC4 are the postcodes of the City of London, the financial district, so 'city' gives EC. The '8' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking guide lists ingredients and steps, a set of directions.

clue.text: One pegged 14 underwear I left? Very nearly

parts.note: long johns are full-length underpants

indicators.note: nearly means not quite whole, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: very taken in full, before being cut

explanation.surface: Someone with clothes on a line leaving their underwear almost entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One pegged' sounds like washing on a line, but it means a man with a wooden peg leg, the pirate of Treasure Island. 'nearly' cuts VERY to VER. The '14' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-legged pirate in Stevenson's novel walked on a wooden leg, a peg.

clue.text: Clearly showing no awareness, left one out

indicators.note: out means removed, so these letters are taken from the longer word

parts.note: acting unaware of one's surroundings is acting obliviously
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone plainly unaware that they left one person out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L and I from OBLIVIOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done evidently or plainly is done in a manifest way.

clue.text: Instrument changed into something offensive

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: changed means the little word that follows is rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical instrument transformed into something offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument changed' looks like one idea, but 'changed' governs only the next word, 'into'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of a rule or law is an offence.

clue.text: Failure to use decimal 15 notation is a matter of perspective

explanation.surface: A complaint about bad decimal notation that turns out to be subjective.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a decimal point that disappears; in drawing, the spot where parallel lines seem to meet. The '15' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping the dot in decimals makes it go missing, and in art the perspective lines converge on one spot.

clue.text: Reporter's assertion is to look good

explanation.surface: A journalist's claim about appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I'M PRESS, it is what a reporter says to get access; the other sense is to make a good impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist announcing their media status says they are the papers, and to win admiration is to make a fine showing.

clue.text: Scientist, British, not 17 working at home

parts.note: a machine that is not working is off
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A British researcher who is not at work but at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The '17' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A boffin is British slang for a research scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: One's lucky to see part of a whale

explanation.surface: Someone fortunate enough to glimpse a whale.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a stroke of luck; the other is a lobe of a whale's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky chance success is a fluke, and each flat lobe of a whale's tail bears the same name.

clue.text: Friend ashen after 19 absorbing book, that's very clear

indicators.note: after means this comes later than the friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something inside

parts.note: an ashen face is pale

explanation.surface: A friend turned grey after being absorbed in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts B inside PALE. The '19' is a printing artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palpable can almost be touched, so it is plain or obvious.

clue.text: Member getting nothing causes indecisive state

parts.note: a limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A club member left empty-handed, stuck in uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: Member suggests a club member, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo is to be in an uncertain, unresolved condition.

clue.text: Various clues to a word meaning 'kiss'

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the words clues to a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of crossword clues leading to a word for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' looks like it describes the clues, but it rearranges CLUES TO A.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is the formal or humorous word for to plant one's lips on someone.

clue.text: Germany's leader brought in a munition, backing wartime device

indicators.note: backing means the whole is read in reverse
brought in means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a mine is an explosive munition

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Germany's

explanation.surface: A German commander bringing in arms to support a wartime machine.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes into A MINE to give AMGINE, and 'backing' turns it round. The Enigma was the German cipher machine of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigma was the cipher machine the Germans used to encode messages in the Second World War.

clue.text: Some natty retread?

indicators.note: some means only part of the words natty retread is taken

explanation.surface: A smart refurbished wheel covering.
explanation.walkthrough: A retread is a tyre given new tread, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a worn wheel covering with fresh rubber added.

clue.text: Nancy is on board first of yachts

indicators.note: on, read with board, means aboard a vessel, so the little word goes within the ship

parts.note: board stands for a ship one goes aboard, and SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word yachts

explanation.surface: Someone called Nancy sailing aboard the leading yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a girl's name but is dated slang for an effeminate man. 'On board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are dated, often derogatory slang for a timid or effeminate male.

clue.text: No cricket side will have twelve

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team that will never have twelve players.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs. A team has eleven players, so 'twelve' tempts as a count; it is the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the day is midday.
